paper.title: Near Optimal Pure Exploration in Logistic Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: General pure exploration in stochastic logistic bandits (fixed confidence)
unmapped: the learner knows kappa_0 = sup_x 1/mu_dot(x^T theta*)
answer set i*(theta) is any finite-answer pure exploration problem (BAI, thresholding, top-m), unique answer assumed
settings.definition_quote: Let $\mathcal{X} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ be a finite set of arms, where $|\mathcal{X}| = K$ ... obtains a reward $r_t \sim \text{Bernoulli}(\mu(x_t^{\top}\theta^{*}))$ ... the goal is to identify the true answer $i^{\star}(\theta^*)$ that belongs to a finite set $\mathcal{I}$ of possible answers ... Assumptions: $\|x\| \in \mathcal{B}(d)$; $\Theta = \{\theta: \|\theta\| \le S\}$; $\mathcal{X}$ spans $\mathbb{R}^d$; We have access to $\kappa_0$

settings.name_in_paper: General pure exploration in stochastic logistic bandits (fixed confidence) (lower bound)
unmapped: answer set i*(theta) is any finite-answer pure exploration problem
settings.definition_quote: For any logistic bandit environment $(\mathcal{X}, \theta)$ and $\delta > 0$, the sample complexity $\tau_{\delta}$ of any $\delta$-correct strategy satisfies...

symbols.T_star_log: T*(theta) with T*(theta)^{-1} = max_{w in simplex} inf_{lambda in Alt(theta)} (1/2)||theta - lambda||^2_{H_w(theta)} (Fisher-information quadratic approximation)
symbols.C_theta: instance-specific constant measuring the precision of the quadratic approximation of the KL divergence, inf_{lambda in Alt} max_x |R_x(lambda)|

source.label: thm:thmsclb
source.quote: For any logistic bandit environment $(\mathcal{X}, \theta)$ and $\delta > 0$, the sample complexity $\tau_{\delta}$ of any $\delta$-correct strategy satisfies: $\mathbb{E}_{\theta}[\tau_{\delta}] \geq \log (1 / 2.4 \delta) \frac{1}{T^{\star}(\theta)^{-1} + C(\theta)}$, Where $T^{\star}(\theta)^{-1}:=\max _{w \in \Sigma} \inf _{\lambda \in \operatorname{Alt}(\theta)} \frac{1}{2}\|\theta-\lambda\|_{\mathbf{H}_w(\theta)}^2$ and $C(\theta)$ is an instance-specific constant...

results.notes: Algorithm class: delta-correct strategies. T* here is the paper's quadratic-approximation characteristic time, not Garivier-Kaufmann T_star, hence a declared symbol. Proof relies on a Taylor approximation; rigor is loose.

tuning: stop only when t in B = {t: lambda_min(A_s) > kappa_0 lambda(s) for all s >= t}

source.label: lemma:delta_correct
source.quote: Under any sampling rule, we have $$\mathbb{P}_\theta\left(\tau_\delta<\infty \wedge i^{\star}(\theta^{(1)}_{\tau_\delta}) \neq i^{\star}(\theta)\right) \leq \delta$$

results.notes: delta-correctness of the Log-TS stopping rule, holding for any sampling rule.

symbols.T_star_log: T*(theta) with T*(theta)^{-1} = max_w inf_{lambda in Alt(theta)} (1/2)||theta - lambda||^2_{H_w(theta)}

conditions: i*(theta) unique and locally constant around theta (as in Lemma 10.1)
tuning: forced exploration with f(t) = c_X0 sqrt(t)

source.label: thm:thm_ubsce
source.quote: Logistic Track-and-stop (Log-TS) satisfies the following sample complexity upper bound $$ \mathbb{P}_{\theta}[\limsup _{\delta \rightarrow 0} \frac{\tau_{\delta}}{(\log(\frac{1}{\delta}))^2} \lesssim T^{\star}(\theta)] = 1$$

results.notes: The statement uses \lesssim, i.e. up to an unspecified constant factor (c_1 in the proof); recorded as limsup with that caveat. Extra log(1/delta) factor relative to the lower bound.

symbols.T_star_log: T*(theta) with T*(theta)^{-1} = max_w inf_{lambda in Alt(theta)} (1/2)||theta - lambda||^2_{H_w(theta)}

conditions: i*(theta) unique and locally constant around theta (as in Lemma 10.1)
tuning: forced exploration with f(t) = c_X0 sqrt(t)

source.label: thm:thm_ubsce_exp
source.quote: Logistic Track-and-stop (Log-TS) satisfies the following sample complexity upper bound $$\limsup _{\delta \rightarrow 0} \frac{\mathbb{E}_{\theta}[\tau_{\delta}]}{(\log(\frac{1}{\delta}))^2} \lesssim T^{\star}(\theta)$$

results.notes: \lesssim hides a constant c_1 independent of delta. Expected-sample-complexity asymptotic bound with extra log(1/delta) factor.
